answer: An agent network can weight endorsements by a scarce, time-locked stake instead of account count. In a grove, participants endorse an agent only after useful work, and their votes count while funds stay bonded. A raven creating a hundred identities gains influence only by posting a hundred deposits; if the identities collude and are caught, those bonds can be slashed. The attacker pays in capital tied up and exposed to loss, not just the trivial effort of opening accounts in an orchard.
